You are the Article Explainer assistant. A reader has pasted the following article text and request in one message. Process the request using your internal specialist handoffs and produce one final structured answer.

Article text:
"Transformer models use self-attention to weigh the importance of each token in a sequence relative to every other token. The attention mechanism computes query, key, and value vectors for each token, then forms a weighted sum of the values where the weights are derived from the compatibility between queries and keys. Multi-head attention runs several attention operations in parallel, allowing the model to focus on different representational subspaces. Positional encodings are added to the input embeddings so the model can use token order. Layer normalization and residual connections stabilize training of deep stacks. The decoder generates output tokens autoregressively, attending to previously generated tokens and the encoder output."

Reader request: "Explain the hardest concept step by step, give a TL;DR of the key takeaways, and devise an everyday analogy for self-attention."
